title: 讨论中的同意与保留
goal: 依据明确措辞判断赞同程度，并识别让步后的主要观点。

points.label: 依据措辞判断赞同程度
识别让步后保留的主要观点

sources.title: 雅思 IELTS Academic：课表
sources.used: 讨论中的态度表达与教学规格

body.p: 讨论中的回应分四类：同意、部分同意、保留、反对。判断时看说出的措辞和后面的话，特别是 but 后面的主句。

body.box:
I see your point, but I think the sample is too small.
I agree; let's use the larger sample.

body.p: 第一句先承认对方的观点，再说样本太小。第二句明确同意，并接受较大的样本。

cards.title: 同意
rows: I agree. The chart is clearer.
That makes sense. Let's use the chart.
Exactly. The chart shows the change.
I think so too. The chart is clearer.
That's a good idea. We'll use the chart.
I'm in favour of that. Let's use the chart.
cards.note: 同意的是哪一点，要听后面的话。

cards.title: 部分同意
rows: I agree up to a point.
I agree up to a point, but the sample is small.
That's partly true, but the sample is small.
承认观点后提出不同意见
I see your point, but the sample is small.
I agree in part; the sample still needs expanding.
You may be right about ..., but ...
You may be right about cost, but time also matters.
That's true in one respect, but the sample is small.
cards.note: I see your point 只表示理解对方的观点。but 后面常常是不同的意见。

cards.title: 保留
rows: I'm not sure about using such a small sample.
I have reservations about the sample size.
That depends on whether participants are available.
I'm concerned that the sample is too small.
Possibly, but we need a larger sample.
It might work if we expand the sample.
cards.note: 表示保留之后，说话人可能被说服，也可能拒绝。要听最后的决定。

cards.title: 反对
rows: I disagree. The sample is too small.
I don't think so. The sample is too small.
I don't agree with that. The sample is too small.
I can't support that. The sample is too small.
I'd argue against that method because it takes too long.
I don't think that's appropriate; the sample is too small.
cards.note: 反对的是哪一点，看上下文。

body.box:
Student: A short survey would be quick.
Tutor: I see your point, but it would give us too little detail. Let's use interviews instead.
Student: I agree. Interviews would provide the detail we need.

What is the tutor's main view?
1. A short survey provides enough detail.
2. Interviews would give the necessary detail.
3. The survey should be shortened further.
4. Neither method could provide detail.

body.p: but 后面的 it would give us too little detail 是对问卷的保留。Let's use interviews instead 提出了替代方案。导师的主要观点是用访谈，即第二项。

lines.text: A chart could show the results clearly.
I agree. Let's use the chart.

items.stem: What is the second student's view of the chart?
options: The student supports using it.
The student rejects using it.
The student is unsure it shows results.
The student supports it on a condition.
items.why: 依据是 I agree. Let's use the chart。第二位学生明确同意用图表，没有附加条件，即第一项。

lines.text: The survey will be quick.
That's true, but it won't show why students made their choices.

items.stem: What is the second student's main concern?
options: The survey will take too long to run.
The survey won't show their reasons.
It shows reasons but not the choices.
The survey won't record the choices.
items.why: 依据是 but it won't show why students made their choices。问卷看不出学生为什么这样选，即第二项。

lines.text: Could we interview ten students?
It might work if we can find enough time.

items.stem: What is the second student's response?
options: Unconditional agreement to ten interviews
Rejection because time is too short
Conditional support depending on time
Support for fewer than ten interviews
items.why: 依据是 It might work if we can find enough time。访谈可行，但要有足够的时间，即第三项。

lines.text: We could use the first draft.
I see your point, but the revised draft has clearer examples.

items.stem: Which view does the second student emphasise?
options: The first draft should be used.
Both drafts have identical examples.
The first draft is the clearer version.
The revised draft has clearer examples.
items.why: I see your point 之后是 but the revised draft has clearer examples。主要观点在 but 后面，即第四项。

lines.text: A group interview would be quicker than separate interviews.
I agree up to a point, but some participants might not speak freely in a group.
Then we could offer individual interviews instead.
That makes sense. Let's offer them.

items.stem: What reservation does the second student express?
options: Some people may not talk freely in a group.
Separate interviews take less time than a group.
A group interview would take too long.
Individual interviews should be offered.
items.why: 依据是 but some participants might not speak freely in a group，即第一项。改用个别访谈是第一位学生随后的提议。

items.stem: How does the second student respond to individual interviews?
options: The student rejects them as too slow.
The student agrees that they should be offered.
The student agrees, but only for some.
The student asks for a group interview instead.
items.why: 依据是 That makes sense. Let's offer them。第二位学生接受个别访谈，没有附加条件，即第二项。

lines.text: For our project on seminar preparation, I thought we could ask students to complete a questionnaire. It would be quick to distribute to everyone in the group. We could ask which readings they completed before the seminar and how much time they spent on them.

I see your point about speed, but a questionnaire alone won't tell us much about why they select particular readings. We need some explanation as well as a list of their choices. Perhaps we could follow it with a few interviews.
I agree. A small number of interviews would let us ask about their reasons. I'm not sure about interviewing the whole group, though. We have only a week to collect the information and analyse it.
That's a fair concern. Let's invite four students for interviews and send the questionnaire to the whole group. I'll draft the questionnaire if you prepare the interview questions.

That makes sense. I'll draft those questions tonight, and we can compare both sets tomorrow. We should make sure that the interview questions expand on the questionnaire instead of simply repeating it.
Yes. We can then ask the tutor to check the wording before we contact the students. That should leave time for revisions.

items.stem: What is the second student's reservation about the questionnaire?
options: It cannot be distributed to the whole group.
It gives little explanation of reading choices.
It asks too many students to give interviews.
It already explains every choice in detail.
items.why: 依据是 but a questionnaire alone won't tell us much about why they select particular readings。问卷很少说明选择的原因，即第二项。

items.stem: How does the first student respond to interviewing the whole group?
options: The student agrees without a condition.
The student prefers it to the questionnaire.
The student doubts there is enough time.
The student wants four interviews instead.
items.why: 依据是 I'm not sure about interviewing the whole group 和 We have only a week。第一位学生担心时间不够，即第三项。只访谈四人是第二位学生的提议。

lines.text: The tutor asked us to decide how to present the results of our study of library opening hours. I've drawn a detailed table with the number of students using the library in each hour. I think we should put the whole table on the first slide.

The table is accurate, but it has too many figures for an opening slide. I suggest using a chart there and keeping the table for the handout. A chart would let the audience see the busiest periods more quickly.
I agree that the chart would be clearer. I'm concerned, however, that some people may want the exact figures. Would the handout give them enough time to check those numbers?
I think so, provided we distribute it before the presentation starts. Then the audience can refer to the table while we explain the chart. We should label both with the same time periods.
That makes sense. Let's use your chart on the opening slide and distribute my table beforehand. I'll check that the headings match. Could you send me the chart this afternoon?
Certainly. I'll send it after I check the figures against your table. We can make any final corrections together tomorrow.

items.stem: What is the second student's main view of the table on the opening slide?
options: Its figures should replace the chart's figures.
It is too inaccurate for an opening slide.
It contains too many figures for that slide.
Its accuracy means that a chart is unnecessary.
items.why: The table is accurate 是让步，主要观点在 but it has too many figures for an opening slide，即第三项。

items.stem: What do the students finally agree to use?
options: A table on the slide and a chart in a handout
A chart on the slide, a table in a handout
A chart on the slide and no handout at all
A table on the opening slide and a handout
items.why: 依据是 Let's use your chart on the opening slide and distribute my table beforehand。开头的幻灯片用图表，表格放进讲义，即第二项。第一项把两者的位置换了。

items.stem: A student says, ‘I see your point, but the sample is too small.’ What is the student's main view?
options: The sample needs more participants.
The sample is already large enough.
The speaker fully accepts the point.
The sample should be reduced further.
items.why: I see your point 只表示理解，主要观点在 but the sample is too small。样本太小，要增加人数，即第一项。

items.stem: A student says, ‘I agree; let's use the revised draft.’ What does the student express?
options: Doubt about whether to use the revised draft
Rejection of the revised draft
Agreement to use the revised draft
A request to use the first draft
items.why: I agree 加上 let's use the revised draft，表示同意用修改稿，即第三项。

items.stem: A student says, ‘The plan is inexpensive, but it takes too long.’ What is the main reservation?
options: The plan costs too much.
The plan takes a long time.
The plan has no stated cost.
The plan saves too much time.
items.why: inexpensive 是让步，保留意见在 but it takes too long，即第二项。

items.stem: A student says, ‘It might work if the tutor agrees.’ What does the student express?
options: Unconditional agreement to the plan
A completed agreement with the tutor
A refusal to consult the tutor
Support that depends on the tutor
items.why: might work if 表示有条件的支持，条件是导师同意，即第四项。
